name: Otter Browser
basedOn: Qt (QtWebEngine, Chromium-based; QtWebKit backend also exists)
statusNote: Last stable 1.0.03 (Feb 2022) and last SourceForge builds June 2022; the maintainer still commits almost daily and a Qt6 port is in progress. FreeBSD dropped its port in Sep 2026 because the Qt5 WebEngine is deprecated.

version.upstream: Qt5 / QtWebEngine (Chromium version depends on system Qt)

updateCadence: No stable release since Feb 2022; daily git commits and weekly progress reports
pitch: Qt browser that recreates Opera 12's customisable UI. Stable releases stopped in 2022.
summary: A Qt5 browser that recreates classic Opera 12: configurable toolbars and shortcuts, mouse gestures, notes, feeds and a content blocker. Development goes on in git, but the last stable release dates from 2022.
bestFor: Fans of classic Opera 12 who want its customisable layout back
Power users who want mouse gestures, notes, a feed reader and sidebars built in
People happy to build from git or use a distro package
notFor: Anyone who needs timely Chromium security fixes
Users who want browser extensions or sync
Beginners who want a one-click installer on Windows or macOS

pros.title: Opera 12 heritage
pros.detail: Aims to recreate the best aspects of Opera 12.x with a modular, highly configurable interface.

pros.title: Built-in tools
pros.detail: Includes an RSS/Atom feeds reader, notes, content blocker, session management, password manager and userscript support.

pros.title: Fully configurable
pros.detail: Toolbars, menus, shortcuts and mouse gestures can be rearranged and remapped.

pros.title: No telemetry known
pros.detail: Volunteer project with no business model and no data-collection service.

pros.title: Wide platform reach
pros.detail: Runs on Linux, BSD, macOS, Windows, Haiku, RISC OS and OS/2 or ArcaOS.

cons.title: No release since 2022
cons.detail: Stable 1.0.03 shipped on 2022-02-22 and the last SourceForge build dates from June 2022.

cons.title: Qt5 dead end
cons.detail: The project still builds against Qt 5.15; FreeBSD removed its port in Sep 2026 as it depends on the deprecated Qt5 WebEngine.

cons.title: Slow security patches
cons.detail: Chromium fixes arrive only through the system Qt WebEngine, which for Qt5 is no longer actively developed.

cons.title: No extension system
cons.detail: There is no extension API; only userscripts and built-in tools.

faq.a: Partly. The maintainer commits to git almost daily and posts weekly reports, but the last stable release was 1.0.03 on 2022-02-22.

faq.q: Does Otter have a Qt6 version?
faq.a: A Qt6 port is under way (weekly report #638 of 2026-03-30 says it is getting closer), but no Qt6 release has been published.
No. Otter has no extension API; it offers userscripts and its own built-in tools.

timeline.event: Initial Qt6 port work begins (weekly report #548)
Weekly report #638 says the Qt6 port is getting closer
FreeBSD removes its port: not ported to Qt6, depends on deprecated Qt5 WebEngine

switching.note: Imports and exports bookmarks (HTML) and has an OPML importer for feeds; passwords and extensions do not carry over.

privacy.defaults: Content blocking profiles and Do Not Track available; no telemetry known; no fingerprint defences

spec.defaultSearch: Configurable list of bundled engines (default unverified)
spec.drm: None by default (depends on Qt WebEngine build)
spec.codecs: Depends on the system Qt WebEngine and GStreamer build
spec.patchLag: Follows the system Qt5 WebEngine, which is deprecated

windows.minOs: Windows (installers and an XP zip listed historically)
notes: Binaries come from SourceForge; SourceForge shows nothing newer than June 2022
DMG builds were announced in release news; current availability unverified
1.0.03 packaged by Fedora, openSUSE, Void and others
AppImage on SourceForge; BSD, Haiku, RISC OS and OS/2 ports also exist

trackingProtection: Content blocking profiles; Do Not Track
cookieIsolation: Per-site cookie rules and a cookie panel
adBlocker: Content blocking profiles with ABP-style lists
verticalTabs: Tab bar position is configurable; true vertical layout unverified
webPanels: Sidebar with built-in panels (bookmarks, notes, history, links)
mailCalendarRss: Feeds reader (Atom/RSS 2.0, OPML import); no mail or calendar

jsSpeed: Qt5 WebEngine is an older Chromium V8
graphics: WebGL via old QtWebEngine; no WebGPU
lowEnd: Needs Qt5 WebEngine; heavier than Falkon-class
installSize: Small app but large Qt WebEngine dependency
privacyDefaults: No telemetry, blocking available but opt-in
securityHardening: Chromium sandbox, but dated Qt5 WebEngine base
patchSpeed: Depends on deprecated Qt5 WebEngine updates
lookCustom: Configurable toolbars and skins; limited theming
advancedSettings: Large settings dialog and config editor
tabManagement: Pinned tabs, tab bar placement, sessions; no groups
searchFreedom: Many bundled engines, custom ones easy
media: Codecs depend on the Qt build; no DRM
longevity: One maintainer, no release since 2022, Qt5 dead end
beginnerFriendly: Familiar UI but no easy current installer
